solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the blog titled it No 21952, which the sequence puts at 29152

clue.text: No great distance to north: others on the move in south-west

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside
letters that are on the move will not stay in the order given

parts.note: TO + N (north) + OTHERS, rearranged
W for west, the compass point, closing the shell
S for south, the compass point, opening the outer shell

explanation.surface: Directions for a short walk: nip north, while the others wander about down in the south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is fodder, not a link: the anagram takes TO, N and OTHERS together, and the result sits between the two halves of south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the distance you could lob a stone, so a very short way.

clue.text: Short jacket turned up in bag

indicators.note: a word that is short falls one letter shy of full length
in a down clue, turning up reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: CASE, a jacket or casing, cut short

explanation.surface: A cropped jacket has turned up stuffed in someone's bag.
explanation.walkthrough: A jacket in the potato or book sense is an outer case, which is the synonym needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from biology: a pouch-like cavity in a plant or animal.

clue.text: Magical land with a certain invigorating air

parts.note: the land of the Wizard of Oz
'a certain' person is 'one'

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale land with a bracing atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: The Victorians believed the sharp smell of the seaside was a gas that did you good, and the name stuck to fresh, bracing air.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose, informal sense: the fresh, stimulating air of the seaside.

clue.text: Perhaps Gladstone's rising importance in surrounding area?

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: Gladstone is an example of the answer

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: note means importance, as in a person of note

indicators.note: surrounding means the word in goes around the letter for area

explanation.surface: Does the prime minister's growing stature come from where he lives?
explanation.walkthrough: William Gladstone, the Victorian prime minister, went to Eton College.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladstone was educated at Eton, so he is an example of an old boy of that school.

clue.text: Display too much creative work around restaurant

indicators.note: turned around, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: to air something is to display it
over the top
art is creative work

explanation.surface: Someone is overdoing the artwork on show in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' comes last and governs everything before it, not just the nearest word.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the informal, family-run Italian eating house.

clue.text: River Fleet swelled with hot eastern current

indicators.note: something swelled with extra matter grows to hold it inside

parts.note: the Royal Navy, split to hold the rest
H (hot) + E (eastern) + I (current, the symbol in physics)

explanation.surface: The Fleet, a London river, swells with a warm current from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fleet is a buried river in London, which makes it look like part of the definition; here it is the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: The German spelling of the Rhine, Europe's great river.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing succeeded entering temple on lake

indicators.note: entering puts the letter for succeeded inside the word for temple

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
re means on or concerning
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A layabout made it into a lakeside temple.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is an idle, worthless person.

clue.text: Lost bird taking off close to castle ditch

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, and taking it off removes the last letter

parts.note: a castle's ditch, minus its last letter T

explanation.surface: A bird wanders off from a castle moat.
explanation.walkthrough: The giant flightless bird of New Zealand was hunted out centuries ago, which is why it is 'lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost here means extinct: the giant New Zealand bird died out around 1400.

clue.text: Kinky game involving a learner in study in college

indicators.note: involving means the rearranged letters wrap around the rest
kinky means twisted, so the letters of game are bent into a new order
in puts A and L inside the word for study

parts.note: a den is a private study
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: An odd game with a student going on in a college room.
explanation.walkthrough: Two operations nest here: the study takes in the learner, and the twisted game takes in that result.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalene is a college of Cambridge University.

clue.text: Immortal heart in a man at sea

indicators.note: confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: A man at sea whose heart will never die.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'heart in a man' is fodder, even though 'in' looks like a container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for undying, from the amaranth, a legendary flower that never fades.

clue.text: Clown dead having consumed hot bean product

indicators.note: what has been consumed is inside

parts.note: Coco the Clown, a famous circus clown
H for hot, as on taps
the late someone is dead

explanation.surface: A clown has died after eating a hot bean dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The clown takes H before LATE follows, though the clue names 'dead' first. Cocoa beans are the beans in question, not baked beans.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: it is made from roasted cacao beans.

clue.text: Athenian character making the case for Simonides?

definitions.meaning: the surface wants a person from Athens; the setter means a Greek letter
the surface wants a lawyer defending the poet; the setter means the Greek S, which begins and ends SimonideS, its case

explanation.surface: An Athenian personality stands up to argue in defence of the poet Simonides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means letter and 'case' means the outer letters of a word, so the Greek S is the letter that encloses the Greek poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the Greek S, a letter Athenians wrote, and it opens and closes Simonides.

clue.text: Boots perhaps initially muddy I placed in trunk

indicators.note: placed in puts the letters inside the word for trunk

parts.note: a trunk is a large storage chest

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of muddy

explanation.surface: Dirty boots are stowed in the trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots looks like footwear, but here it is Boots, the British high-street pharmacy chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Boots is a UK chain of pharmacies, so it is an example of a pharmacist's shop.

clue.text: Demand the writer's rough and hearty in old game show

parts.note: to call for is to demand
the writer is me, so the writer's is my
a bluff manner is rough and hearty

explanation.surface: Someone demands a blunt, hearty tone from the author of a TV quiz script.
explanation.walkthrough: The long-running BBC panel game had teams offering true and false definitions of obscure words.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper name: the BBC panel game that ran on and off from 1965 to 2005.

clue.text: Enlightened state's new stories written on Irish victory

indicators.note: in an across clue, words written on another follow it

parts.note: N for new
abbreviation for Irish
V for victory
ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories

explanation.surface: A state that has become enlightened publishes new tales about an Irish triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: Ana, a collection of sayings or anecdotes, is a crossword staple; it survives as the ending in words like Victoriana.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious term: in Buddhism, the final state of perfect enlightenment and release.

clue.text: Bloom left sharp object after first part of Ulysses

indicators.note: in an across clue, what comes after is written to the right
the first part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: L for left
the first letter of Ulysses
a pin is sharp

explanation.surface: Leopold Bloom leaves a sharp object near the opening of James Joyce's Ulysses.
explanation.walkthrough: Leopold Bloom is the hero of Joyce's Ulysses, so the surface reads as literary criticism; Bloom here is just a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a tall garden flower with spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Contestant's history embracing life cut short?

indicators.note: the past embraces, so holds inside, the shortened word

parts.note: history is the past

indicators.note: the word for life is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: 'not on your nellie' means 'not on your life', so nellie stands for life

explanation.surface: A competitor whose record includes a life ended early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on your nellie' is British slang for 'certainly not', a variant of 'not on your life', which is how nellie can stand for life.
explanation.definitionFit: A panellist sits on a quiz or game-show panel, so is one of the contestants.

clue.text: Hardy's villain periodically consumed by envy?

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the answer is hardy

indicators.note: consumed by means the picked letters are swallowed inside the word for envy

parts.note: to resent someone's success is to envy it

indicators.note: periodically means taking every other letter of villain

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy villain is eaten up by jealousy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy's villain' suggests a character from Thomas Hardy, but 'Hardy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy and resilient both describe someone tough and able to recover from hardship.

clue.text: Wise man covers relic damaged in desecration

indicators.note: covers means the word for wise man goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

indicators.note: damaged indicates the letters of relic are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A wise man shields a broken relic from an act of profanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilege is the violation of something sacred.

clue.text: Mr White in Chamonix around on time to see attraction there?

indicators.note: to go around something is to enclose it

parts.note: M for Monsieur, the French Mr
French for white
ON + T (time)

explanation.surface: A Monsieur Blanc in Chamonix, turning up on time to go sightseeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamonix' makes both Mr and White French: M. Blanc. 'There' points back to Chamonix, the resort beneath the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by location: Western Europe's highest peak towers over Chamonix and draws its visitors.

clue.text: Pierce and Oscar separating horse from trap

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
O in the NATO alphabet
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: Pierce and Oscar step in to part a horse from its carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierce looks like a man's name to go with Oscar; it is the verb. A trap is also a light horse-drawn cart, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb from the weapon: to stab with the blade fixed to a rifle.

clue.text: Something fragrant consecutive characters brought to India

parts.note: EL and EM, the letters L and M spelt out, next to each other in the alphabet
I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A string of scented goods shipped to India.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters can be spelt out as words: EL, EM, EN and so on. Any neighbouring pair is 'consecutive characters'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a fragrant tree resin used in perfumes and varnishes.

clue.text: Returning piano taken into first-rate city shops

indicators.note: going back the way it came, so the whole string reads upwards

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate

indicators.note: something taken into another is put inside it

parts.note: the city, split to hold P
p for piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A piano sent back is accepted into the city's best shops.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written with I standing for 1, a common crossword swap.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural: large stores, the Latin plural of emporium.

clue.text: Corporation finished in such a position?

parts.note: a corporation is an old joke word for a pot belly
time's up: finished

explanation.surface: A company that has gone bust.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a business failing, which is what going belly-up means; 'such a position' is lying on your back, like a dead fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: dead fish float on their backs, so a failed company is said to go this way.

clue.text: One in wheeled carriage brings dad to Paris

indicators.note: what sits in a pram is inside it

parts.note: a baby's pram, split to hold I
the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A dad pushes a baby in a pram on a trip to Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is the Trojan prince, not the French city: his father was the King of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek myth: the King of Troy fathered Paris, whose elopement with Helen began the Trojan War.

clue.text: Progress here impossible, four to leave showing no emotion

indicators.note: letters that leave a word depart from it

parts.note: impassive means showing no emotion
the Roman numeral, removed

explanation.surface: A deadlock where four people walk out stony-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: Four is a Roman numeral here, not a head count.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a deadlock or dead end, where nobody can move forward.

clue.text: Two short ways to make wooden strip

parts.note: ST, short for street
AVE, short for avenue

explanation.surface: Two shortcuts to making a strip of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two short ways' gives both pieces: two abbreviated road names.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain sense: one of the curved wooden planks that make up a barrel.

clue.text: Something nasty afoot where bachelor joins this association?

indicators.note: the letter joins the answer to make the thing named, so the answer is that thing with the letter taken away

parts.note: a painful swelling on the foot
B for bachelor, removed

explanation.surface: Something nasty is going on, where a single man signs up to this society.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: add B to the answer and you get BUNION. 'Afoot' is literal: on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a trade union or club is an association of members.

clue.text: Drunk from Britain fuddled with Ecstasy twice

indicators.note: twice means the letter for ecstasy is used a second time, after the rest
fuddled means confused, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone from Britain confused after taking ecstasy twice is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: BRITAIN plus two Es is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a drunk, a person habitually intoxicated.

clue.text: Partake of repast odd characters have left

indicators.note: the odd letters go, leaving the even ones

parts.note: the even letters of rEpAsT

explanation.surface: Guests share a meal after the strange characters have gone home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' reads as eccentric people leaving; it means letters 1, 3 and 5.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to partake of food is to consume it.

clue.text: Corpulent Liberal to be extracted from apartment

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
L for Liberal, removed

explanation.surface: An overweight Liberal politician is to be evicted from his flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberals were a major British party, and L is their standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: corpulent is the formal word for having a large, stout body.

clue.text: Character to invite round guys on time

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it

parts.note: to invite, as in to tempt fate; split to hold the rest

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another is written after it

parts.note: an era is a period of time
guys are men

explanation.surface: A question of whether it is in someone's nature to have the lads round in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On time' is not ON + T here: 'on' is a placement word, and the T comes from the end of tempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a person's nature or disposition.
